content.title: THE MINERAL YOUR {{THYROID}} IS BEGGING YOU FOR
facts: Without enough iodine your thyroid can't make the hormones that set your metabolism speed, so energy and body temperature quietly drop.
Manganese activates the enzymes that stitch together the collagen framework inside bone and cartilage, so joints stay cushioned.
**Copper** (Iron's Partner) — Oysters | Cashews | Shiitake Mushrooms | Dark Turkey Meat
Copper helps your body actually absorb and use iron, meaning low copper can leave you feeling drained even if your iron intake looks fine.
**Selenium** (Cell Shield) — Brazil Nuts (1-2/day) | Tuna | Turkey | Eggs
Selenium powers an antioxidant enzyme that protects your cells from daily wear and tear, especially in the thyroid itself.
**Chromium** (Blood Sugar Helper) — Broccoli | Green Beans | Turkey Breast | Grapes
Chromium helps insulin do its job more efficiently, which can smooth out energy crashes after meals.

caption:
Let's talk about a few of these. Iodine gets almost no attention compared to vitamin D or magnesium, but your thyroid literally cannot produce its hormones without it — and those hormones set the pace for basically every cell's energy use. Copper is the quiet partner mineral most people never hear about: it helps mobilize the iron already in your body, so even a "normal" iron intake can underperform if copper is low. And chromium works behind the scenes with insulin, helping your cells pull glucose out of the blood more smoothly instead of letting it spike and crash. Everyone's body is different, so these are pieces of the puzzle, not a fix-all.
